name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PHOTOSYNTHESIS_SEQUENCING_Q01 - Sequence of electron transfer in Z scheme

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following events of non-cyclic photophosphorylation (Z-scheme) in the correct chronological sequence of electron flow:

  1. Excitation of electrons in the reaction centre \(\text{P}_{700}\) of Photosystem I upon receiving red light.
  2. Transfer of electrons downhill through an electron transport system consisting of cytochromes to Photosystem I.
  3. Excitation of electrons in \(\text{P}_{680}\) of Photosystem II by absorbing \(680\text{ nm}\) light and transfer to an electron acceptor.
  4. Photolysis of water on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane to supply replacement electrons to Photosystem II.
  5. Downhill movement of electrons from an electron acceptor to reduce \(\text{NADP}^+\) to \(\text{NADPH} + \text{H}^+\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle of Non-Cyclic Electron Flow
In the photochemical phase of photosynthesis, the non-cyclic movement of electrons follows a redox potential scale termed the Z-scheme, operating in series between Photosystem II and Photosystem I.

Step 2: Identification of Intermediate Events
Water splitting occurs physically on the inner surface of the thylakoid membrane, supplying continuous replacement electrons to the reaction centre of Photosystem II: \[2\text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow 4\text{H}^+ + \text{O}_2 + 4\text{e}^-\] Simultaneously, the reaction centre chlorophyll a of Photosystem II (\(\text{P}_{680}\)) absorbs red light at \(680\text{ nm}\), causing its electrons to become excited and get transferred uphill to a primary electron acceptor.

Step 3: Intermediate Electron Transport Chain
The primary acceptor passes the electrons downhill along an oxidation-reduction gradient through an electron transport system composed of cytochromes. These electrons do not get used up but are routed directly to the reaction centre of Photosystem I.

Step 4: Excitation at Photosystem I and Final Reduction
Concurrently, reaction centre chlorophyll a of Photosystem I (\(\text{P}_{700}\)) absorbs red light at \(700\text{ nm}\), exciting its electrons, which are transferred to another acceptor with a higher redox potential. Finally, these electrons travel downhill to \(\text{NADP}^+\), where the enzyme \(\text{NADP}\) reductase catalyses the reduction of \(\text{NADP}^+\) to \(\text{NADPH} + \text{H}^+\).

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The correct chronological sequence from start to finish is: photolysis of water to replenish Photosystem II \(\rightarrow\) excitation of \(\text{P}_{680}\) and transfer to an electron acceptor \(\rightarrow\) downhill passage through cytochromes to Photosystem I \(\rightarrow\) excitation of \(\text{P}_{700}\) to another acceptor \(\rightarrow\) downhill reduction of \(\text{NADP}^+\) to \(\text{NADPH} + \text{H}^+\), which corresponds to IV \(\rightarrow\) III \(\rightarrow\) II \(\rightarrow\) I \(\rightarrow\) V.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PHOTOSYNTHESIS_SEQUENCING_Q02 - Sequence of events in C4 dicarboxylic acid pathway

questiontext.text:
Identify the correct logical sequence of stages occurring during the Hatch and Slack (\(\text{C}_4\)) pathway starting from atmospheric carbon dioxide uptake:

  1. Decarboxylation of \(\text{C}_4\) acid in bundle sheath cells releasing \(\text{CO}_2\) and a \(\text{C}_3\) acid.
  2. Carboxylation of phosphoenolpyruvate by \(\text{PEP}\) carboxylase in mesophyll cells to form oxaloacetic acid.
  3. Transport of a \(\text{C}_3\) acid back to mesophyll cells followed by regeneration of phosphoenolpyruvate.
  4. Formation of malic acid or aspartic acid in mesophyll cells and its transport to bundle sheath cells.
  5. Fixation of the released \(\text{CO}_2\) by \(\text{RuBisCO}\) in the Calvin pathway within bundle sheath cells.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle of the Hatch and Slack Pathway
The \(\text{C}_4\) pathway operates across two distinct cell layers—mesophyll cells and bundle sheath cells—exhibiting Kranz anatomy to concentrate \(\text{CO}_2\) around \(\text{RuBisCO}\) and prevent photorespiration.

Step 2: Primary Fixation and Formation of Organic Acids in Mesophyll Cells
Atmospheric \(\text{CO}_2\) dissolves to form bicarbonate ions (\(\text{HCO}_3^-\)) and is accepted by the primary \(3\)-carbon acceptor, phosphoenolpyruvate (\(\text{PEP}\)), catalysed by \(\text{PEP}\) carboxylase in the mesophyll cytosol. This generates the initial \(4\)-carbon acid, oxaloacetic acid (\(\text{OAA}\)).

Step 3: Conversion and Intercellular Transport
Oxaloacetic acid is promptly converted into other \(4\)-carbon dicarboxylic acids, such as malic acid or aspartic acid, within the mesophyll cells. These \(\text{C}_4\) acids are then transported across plasmodesmata into the bundle sheath cells.

Step 4: Decarboxylation and Calvin Cycle Fixation in Bundle Sheath Cells
In the bundle sheath cells, the \(\text{C}_4\) acids undergo enzymatic decarboxylation, releasing \(\text{CO}_2\) and a \(3\)-carbon compound. The elevated concentration of \(\text{CO}_2\) is immediately utilised by \(\text{RuBisCO}\) to enter the standard Calvin (\(\text{C}_3\)) cycle, suppressing the oxygenase activity of \(\text{RuBisCO}\).

Step 5: Transport of C3 Acid and Regeneration of PEP
The residual \(3\)-carbon acid is transported back through plasmodesmata into the mesophyll cells, where it is converted back into phosphoenolpyruvate at the expense of energy, completing the cyclic pathway.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The proper chronological order of events is: \(\text{II}\) (initial carboxylation of \(\text{PEP}\)) \(\rightarrow\) \(\text{IV}\) (conversion to malate/aspartate and transport to bundle sheath) \(\rightarrow\) \(\text{I}\) (decarboxylation releasing \(\text{CO}_2\) and \(\text{C}_3\) acid) \(\rightarrow\) \(\text{V}\) (fixation of \(\text{CO}_2\) by \(\text{RuBisCO}\)) \(\rightarrow\) \(\text{III}\) (transport of \(\text{C}_3\) acid and regeneration of \(\text{PEP}\)).
